quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to driving a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
A motorcycle is easier to see than a car.
You should pass on the shoulder instead of the main road.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
questions.explanation: Visibility is more critical on a motorcycle. A motorcycle's small size makes it easy for other drivers to miss you or for you to disappear into their blind spot.

questions.question: Which item is not considered protective clothing for motorcycle riders?

options.text: A leather jacket
Full-fingered gloves
Long pants made of denim
Athletic shoes

questions.correctAnswerText: Athletic shoes
questions.explanation: A leather jacket, full-fingered gloves, and heavy denim pants protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes that support your ankles instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Use the same lane position at all times.
Change lane positions often to avoid boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you.
Never ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. Choose the lane position that gives you the most space and makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Go faster.
Make sudden movements.
Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: To ride safely on slippery surfaces: slow down, avoid sudden movements, stay away from the road's edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.question: Several factors affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Which one does not?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How quickly a person drinks
Body weight
Height

questions.correctAnswerText: Height
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: Where is the throttle located on a motorcycle?

options.text: Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest
On the left handle grip
On the right handle grip

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: How should you maintain control of your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright.
Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle through a turn, look ahead by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the correct direction.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, ride in:

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass. This position gives you the best view of the passing lane.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Less care than a car.
More care than a car.
Only a mechanic to perform checks.
Service only at a dealer.

questions.correctAnswerText: More care than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: When someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Ignore them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let a tailgater pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers don't expect you there and may leave the road suddenly.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is illegal.
It is slowing down by turning off the engine.
It is slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
It is not recommended because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows you down in a way that is similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, how should they pass?

options.text: Pass in pairs.
Pass in a staggered formation with several riders passing at the same time.
Pass one at a time.
Avoid passing altogether.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass one at a time.
questions.explanation: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, each rider should pass one at a time. The next rider should wait until the first rider has completed their pass.

questions.question: Why should you use your mirrors when stopped at an intersection?

options.text: To see if parked vehicles are entering traffic.
To look for vehicles changing lanes.
To watch for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
To see if someone is planning to turn behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: To watch for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
questions.explanation: When stopped at an intersection, check your mirrors for vehicles approaching from behind. The driver may not see you in time to stop.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
They are caused by worn tires.
They happen in the dark.
They involve riders who have little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders who have little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve inexperienced riders.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Signal and check your mirrors.
Turn your head and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and do a head check to make sure no vehicles are in your way.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: It handles curves about the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It should not be operated in curves.
It should use the shoulder when taking a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: It handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the risk of riding directly alongside another vehicle?

options.text: You can be hidden in the driver's blind spot.
It is better than riding behind the other vehicle.
It is safe because it limits your escape routes.
It should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can be hidden in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding directly alongside another vehicle because the driver may not see you. If the driver does not see you, they may enter your lane without warning. Also, the vehicle can block your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front brake pressed down.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake immediately and apply it smoothly again.

questions.question: Which is NOT a hazard when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: Extended mirrors.
Objects being thrown from other vehicles.
Wind gusts.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the vehicle's mirrors, wind gusts, and objects that may be thrown from the passing vehicle. Headlights are not a hazard when being passed.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help you avoid serious injury?

options.text: A DOT-approved helmet.
Face or eye protection.
Ear buds.
Protective clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: If the roadway is slippery.
If there are only a few vehicles on the roadway.
If the sun is shining.
If drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the roadway is slippery.
questions.explanation: Increase your distance behind other vehicles when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. Leave extra space on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When will a helmet NOT provide the best protection?

options.text: If it is certified by the DOT.
If it fits snugly.
If it is free of defects.
If it has cracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it has cracks.
questions.explanation: A helmet must meet DOT standards and fit snugly for maximum protection. Do not use a helmet with cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Why should you use both the front and rear brakes when slowing or stopping?

options.text: Using only one brake will cause the brakes to wear unevenly.
It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
Using both brakes is the only way to slow down a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes during normal stops creates a habit. This habit will help you in emergencies when using both brakes may be critical.

questions.question: How should you brake on a motorcycle?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab at the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab at the rear brake.
Press down on the front brake and jam on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever and press the rear brake pedal smoothly. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.
